content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a guideline for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults, specifically targeting primary and community care settings. Selection and Appointment of Contributors The Guideline Development Group (GDG) members were identified based on recommendations from the Steering Group and a review of recent authoritative publications, including the Lancet Low Back Pain Series. A total of 31 individuals were contacted, and 25 nominations were received and approved after evaluation. The evaluation process involved independent assessments by two members of the technical unit, who reviewed the nominees' qualifications, skills, and potential conflicts of interest. A two-week public consultation period was also conducted, during which no concerns or comments were submitted. Similarly, the External Review Group (ERG) was formed using the same nomination and selection process. Of the 22 individuals contacted, 17 nominations were received and approved, with 14 members ultimately participating. The ERG reviewed the draft guideline for clarity, factual accuracy, feasibility, and implementation implications but did not alter the recommendations formulated by the GDG. Conflict of Interest Management All contributors, including GDG and ERG members, were required to complete WHO Declaration of Interest (DOI) and Confidentiality Undertaking (CU) forms. These declarations were reviewed by the technical unit in consultation with the Office of Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics. Interests were assessed as insignificant or minimal if they were unlikely to affect the individual's judgment. Where potential conflicts were identified, management strategies included conditional participation, partial exclusion, or total exclusion from specific aspects of the guideline development process. For example: One GDG member was partially excluded from discussions related to an intervention they had contributed to in an evidence synthesis. Another GDG member was recused from discussions on paracetamol (acetaminophen) due to their advisory role with a manufacturer of the drug. Two ERG members were recused from commenting on systemic pharmacotherapies due to their roles on scientific advisory boards and research support from pharmaceutical companies. No other significant conflicts of interest were identified among the remaining GDG or ERG members. No submissions were received during this time. Following the evaluation and consultation period, nominees were formally invited to participate and were required to sign a Memorandum of Agreement and Confidentiality Undertaking. Systematic Review Suppliers and Meeting Observers All contractors contributing to the guideline completed DOI and CU forms, and no significant conflicts of interest were identified. Contractors were prohibited from having financial interests relevant to the guideline's subject matter. Meeting observers also signed confidentiality agreements before attending GDG meetings. Summary of Declarations of Interest The declarations of interest for GDG and ERG members were summarized in tables, with additional biographical information available online. At the start of GDG meetings, members verbally declared any relevant interests, including updates to previous declarations. Since more than 12 months elapsed between the first and second GDG meetings, all members completed new DOI and CU forms in 2022, which were reassessed by the technical unit. Examples of Individual Declarations Jan Hartvigsen: Received research funds for projects on back pain and musculoskeletal conditions, all paid to their employing institution. No private sector funding was involved. The declared interests were not considered significant enough to affect the guideline's credibility. Manuela L. Ferreira: Received research funds for clinical trials on low back pain interventions, including funding from a private sector entity (Medibank Health Research Foundation). These interests were deemed insignificant in terms of risk to the guideline's development. Geoffrey Outerbridge: Declared consultancy with a non-profit organization and retired in 2019. The interests were not considered significant enough to pose any risk to the guideline's credibility. Helen Foster: Received research funds for pediatric musculoskeletal conditions, including from private sector entities (Pfizer, Sanofi Genzyme, AbbVie). She was recused from commenting on systemic pharmacotherapies due to potential conflicts of interest. Conclusion The WHO guideline for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults was developed through a robust and transparent process. All contributors were carefully evaluated for suitability and potential conflicts of interest, with appropriate management strategies implemented where necessary. The guideline aims to provide evidence-based recommendations for managing chronic low back pain in primary and community care settings.
